cards.explanation: The answer is False. Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 14:12), invites them in, and they answer, “we will spend the night in the square.” (Genesis 19:2) They don't say yes right away. Lot has to insist so strongly that they finally follow him into his house (Genesis 19:3).

The answer is feast. Verse 3 says Lot “…prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.” (Genesis 19:3) That's some serious hosting for guests who first said no thanks. I respect a host who goes all out, and I'd bring the cookies.

The answer is that Lot steps outside and shuts the door. “Lot went outside to meet them, shutting the door behind him.” (Genesis 19:6) He goes out to face the whole crowd, and his guests stay behind that door. Honestly, friends, I'd have needed a minute and a cookie first. That's a lot of nerve.

The answer is True. “Please, my brothers…” he pleaded, “don’t do such a wicked thing!” (Genesis 19:7) Lot calls what they want wicked, right to their faces. That takes real nerve with a whole city outside his door.

The answer is that he came as a foreigner and now acts like a judge. The crowd says, “This one came here as a foreigner, and he is already acting like a judge!” (Genesis 19:9) They're saying he's an outsider telling them what to do. Then they threaten to treat him worse than his guests.

The answer is that the two men pull Lot inside and shut the door. “…the men inside reached out, pulled Lot into the house with them, and shut the door.” (Genesis 19:10) The crowd had just pressed in and moved to break down the door (Genesis 19:9). Lot gets pulled to safety right then. I'd like a friend who grabs me at exactly the right second.

The answer is blindness. The men inside “…struck the men at the entrance, young and old, with blindness, so that they wearied themselves trying to find the door.” (Genesis 19:11) A moment before, the crowd was pressing in to break that door down (Genesis 19:9). Now they're wearing themselves out just trying to find it.

The answer is that they are about to destroy the city. The two men say, “…we are about to destroy this place. For the outcry to the LORD against its people is so great that He has sent us to destroy it.” (Genesis 19:13) That's why Lot has to move fast and get his people out. This is the outcry the LORD told Abraham about (Genesis 18:20).

The answer is that they think he is joking. “…his sons-in-law thought he was joking.” (Genesis 19:14) Lot has just told them the LORD is about to destroy the city, and they don't take it seriously. I think this one is heavy, friends, because the warning was real. And the story isn't over.

The answer is hesitates. “…when Lot hesitated, the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters.” (Genesis 19:16) So he slows down instead of hurrying. I can't judge, because I've hit snooze on way smaller emergencies than this one.

The answer is compassion. The men “…led them safely out of the city, because of the LORD’s compassion for them.” (Genesis 19:16) Lot is slow, and they're still led out by the hand. That tells me a lot about the LORD.

The answer is look back. One of the men says, “Run for your lives! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere on the plain!” (Genesis 19:17) Keep your eyes forward and keep moving. Hold on to that order, friends, because it matters in a few verses.

The answer is to flee to a small town nearby. Lot says, “…there is a town nearby where I can flee, and it is a small place.” (Genesis 19:20) He asks for that town instead of the mountains. Then he asks, “…is it not a small place?” and adds, “Then my life will be saved.”

The answer is False. The man says, “I will grant this request as well, and will not demolish the town you indicate.” (Genesis 19:21) Lot gets a yes. Then comes the order to hurry, because the man can't do anything until Lot gets there (Genesis 19:22).

The answer is True, and that's what the text says. “…Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.” (Genesis 19:26) The order had been, “Do not look back…” (Genesis 19:17) This is a heavy verse, so let's take it in quietly.

The answer is smoke rising like smoke from a furnace. Abraham “…saw the smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.” (Genesis 19:28) He's standing in the very place where he had stood before the LORD. It's a quiet, heavy picture.

The answer is Abraham. “…He remembered Abraham, and He brought Lot out of the catastrophe that destroyed the cities where he had lived.” (Genesis 19:29) Lot is Abraham's nephew (Genesis 14:12). Earlier, Abraham had spoken up to the LORD about Sodom (Genesis 18:23-32). The verse puts God remembering Abraham right beside Lot being brought out.

The answer is that Lot is afraid to stay in Zoar. Lot and his daughters “…settled in the mountains—for he was afraid to stay in Zoar—where they lived in a cave.” (Genesis 19:30) That's all the text says about why. I think it's a long way from the feast he cooked in Sodom.

The answer is the Moabites and the Ammonites. The older daughter “…named him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites of today.” The younger “…named him Ben-ammi. He is the father of the Ammonites of today.” (Genesis 19:37-38) This part of the story is heavy, so I'll leave it at that.
